body_markdown:
What does 20 years sound like? As we celebrate[Spotify’s 20th anniversary year](https://newsroom.spotify.com/spotify20/) , that’s the question we put to 20 of our bandmates.


More specifically, we asked to share the songs behind some of their most memorable moments, both in life and at work. The result is a mixtape that offers a glimpse into our history—one memory, one track, and one story at a time.


## Moments close to home


From romantic beginnings to life-changing firsts, these tracks hold cherished personal memories.


### **Tyler** **L • Director, User Fraud**


My wife introduced me to Spotify in 2009, before we were married. For our wedding, we used Spotify to choose the songs and picked


[Elliott Smith](https://open.spotify.com/artist/2ApaG60P4r0yhBoDCGD8YG) ’s cover of “Thirteen” for our first dance.


I’d like to dedicate this song to my wonderful wife, who has always been the most supportive person in my life. She was also the one who helped me pluck up the courage to apply for a job at Spotify in 2011. I can’t wait to see what the next 20 years have in store for us all!


### **Sophie M • Freemium Business Development Lead**


I’ve turned to Spotify at many moments in my life, but the most memorable was the birth of our first child. We created a playlist and listened to it over and over again during pregnancy.[Israel Kamakawiwo’ole](https://open.spotify.com/artist/4ogvuDRerGhZfSf7TtzHlr) ’s cover of “Somewhere Over The Rainbow/What A Wonderful World” was on there, and I vividly remember it playing the moment our son was born. Hearing that song brings back all the happy memories of that day, even now.


### **Becky S • Director Program Management, PZN**


I’d been dating my now-husband for just a month when I invited him to join me on a trip to a music festival six weeks later—which felt very presumptuous! At the festival, it started to rain during


[Raphael Saadiq](https://open.spotify.com/artist/6g0Wah2YFtb1rFgKhUktlo) ’s set, but instead of scattering like most people, we danced together on the deserted bleachers to “Love That Girl.” It was a magical moment and I still feel a rush of new love whenever I hear the song.


### **Lynn R • ​Staff Engineer, Platform**


In an effort to try something new and fulfill a long-held dream of playing onstage, I joined a


[Muse](https://open.spotify.com/artist/12Chz98pHFMPJEknJQMWvI) cover band with a few other Spotifiers. That’s where I met my now-husband! We played “Hysteria” at our wedding.


## The tracks that built us


For many bandmates, certain songs are inseparable from our Spotify journey.


### **Matthew M • Fraud Operations Manager**


I joined Spotify around 2011 and was working in the newly opened Cambridge, U.K., office. We were a small team, all sitting together, and had a shared playlist for the office. At some point, someone added “Careless Whisper” and then… it just never stopped! You’d be deep in work and it would start playing, and people would be laughing (or sighing) across the room. One person would take it off the playlist, and someone else would put it back on. It was just always there.


Every time I hear “Careless Whisper” now, it takes me straight back to that office, the people, and the fun times we had there.


### **Chris S • Senior Product Manager, Experience**


“Uptown Funk (feat. Bruno Mars)” by


[Mark Ronson](https://open.spotify.com/artist/3hv9jJF3adDNsBSIQDqcjp) was everywhere on the radio in 2014, but it wasn’t on Spotify yet. In the U.K., songs often played for weeks before you could stream them. Our small team fought hard to change this, pushing for a simple idea: if a song is on the radio, it should be on Spotify.


It all came to a head with “Uptown Funk,” when


[Fleur East](https://open.spotify.com/artist/37mtx80nMDETlbsq2eFCzc) performed it on TV and her


[cover](https://open.spotify.com/track/75uQYLk1MBGcWjNpPR0AVf?si=cc5d1e9963d84c46) became available before the original. We convinced Sony to release it on Spotify ahead of schedule, and of course it became a massive hit. From that point on, radio and streaming releases aligned, so listeners could get new music right away.


Last year, I worked on our


[SongDNA](https://newsroom.spotify.com/2026-03-24/songdna-announcement-beta/) feature


, and someone chose “Uptown Funk” for our mockups. I spent hours staring at its collaborators and samples but never mentioned that I’d also spent countless hours working on this track back in 2014, or how much it helped change the way music was released.


### **Marcus F • VP Engineering, Music**


In 2014, while working in Stockholm, I was asked to help grow our San Francisco engineering office. To lead the local team, I hired


**Kristian Lindwall** , who graciously agreed to pack up his life and move.


Kristian built an amazing team and brought along many Swedish traditions, including the beloved annual crayfish party. During one of these events, the DJ played a


[Jamie xx](https://open.spotify.com/artist/7A0awCXkE1FtSU8B0qwOJQ) remix of “On Hold.” I fell in love with it and danced alone to it in my hotel room every night of that trip.


It’s become my San Francisco anthem. Hearing it brings back all the effort, joy, and impact of building that office. The drop at 1:58 still sends shivers down my spine and transports me to my old hotel room.


### **Léa D • Associate Director, Advertising Business Marketing EMEA**


Around 10 years ago, an up-and-coming artist named


[Dua Lipa](https://open.spotify.com/artist/6M2wZ9GZgrQXHCFfjv46we) joined us at an event. She spoke on a panel and played a set for maybe 100 people. Most people in the room were just discovering her. I was one of them.


By 2022, she was our beach headliner at


[Cannes](https://newsroom.spotify.com/2022-06-23/all-eyes-on-cannes-lions-spotify-closes-out-an-action-packed-week-on-the-croisette/) , performing on a huge stage in front of a packed crowd. For me, it was a full-circle moment that captures the power of what our platform can do.


### **Lauren SW • Director, Head of Global Social Impact, HR**


I joined the Social Impact team in 2015. Around then, the story of


**Ahmed Mohamed** —a student detained after bringing a homemade clock to school—was everywhere. It was upsetting and sparked a lot of conversation.


As people around the world rallied behind Ahmed, a few of us at Spotify created


[a playlist for Ahmed](https://open.spotify.com/playlist/23qoOKwSAIPv2pHE8zlOQ0) , with songs to encourage and inspire him. We included


[Coldplay](https://open.spotify.com/artist/4gzpq5DPGxSnKTe4SA8HAU) ’s “Clocks” hoping it might make him smile. People from all over eventually found the playlist, shared it, and added their own meaning to it.


That moment shaped how I thought about my work, and it’s something I still come back to. Music can travel quickly, reach widely, and bring people together in ways that feel both personal and shared.


### **Kristin M • Senior House Traffic Manager**


This song defined one of my favorite eras at Spotify. At our 10-year celebration in June 2016, when the song was everywhere, former CEO **Daniel Ek** brought out **[Justin Timberlake](https://open.spotify.com/artist/31TPClRtHm23RisEBtV3X7)** as a surprise guest. It was one of those unforgettable, high-energy moments that perfectly captured the spirit of Spotify. Even now, hearing the song instantly takes me back to that time, those people, and that experience.


## We’re fans, too


At Spotify, we don’t leave our fandom at home. Here are a few stories about the songs that connect our personal passions with our work here.


### **Zach R • Director of Sales, Enterprise Ads**


I’ll never forget my first week using Spotify in 2013. Almost immediately, I was served “Kingdom Come” and “NewYorkSoul” by


[Jon Bellion](https://open.spotify.com/artist/50JJSqHUf2RQ9xsHs0KMHg) . That moment stuck with me—not just because of how much I loved the songs, but because it felt like Spotify instantly understood my taste in a way I hadn’t experienced before.


It’s amazing to look back and realize that Spotify didn’t just introduce me to an artist, it introduced me to a lasting influence on my music taste.


### **Jon C • Senior Engineer, Music**


One of my favorite artists is


[D’Angelo](https://open.spotify.com/artist/336vr2M3Va0FjyvB55lJEd) . Seeing him live was on my concert bucket list, but it never worked out—until, one day, I got an email saying he and his band were performing at our office.


I was in the front row


*.* At the end of the performance, he stepped offstage and shook hands with a few of us (me included!). I snapped a picture of the setlist. By far, one of my favorite musical experiences at the company.


### **Ed C • Senior Staff Engineer, Ads**


I discovered


**Echosmith** when they performed at our old NYC office. When they played “Cool Kids,” I remember thinking about how cool it was to work at Spotify. They were great, and I later went to one of their concerts outside of work.


### **Alex S • Lead, Payments Performance, Markets & Subscriptions**


Watching a close friend grow into an artist has been incredible. Seeing SJU’s music appear on listeners’ playlists makes me proud of both her and where I work. The highlight: watching her play at Slovakia’s biggest festival. Glastonbury next?


### **Karolina** **R • Program Manager, Platform**


During my first months at Spotify, I discovered “Emmylou” by


[First Aid Kit](https://open.spotify.com/artist/21egYD1eInY6bGFcniCRT1) . It quickly became the soundtrack to that chapter of my life: starting a new job, meeting new colleagues, and feeling the excitement of being part of something special.


Whenever I hear it, I’m transported back to those early days and reminded why discovery is such a powerful part of what we build. It’s a simple story, but it captures what Spotify has meant to me—as both a listener and someone who has spent 14 years helping connect people with music that becomes part of their life story.


## The song we played on repeat


For long-tenured bandmates,


[Daft Punk](https://open.spotify.com/artist/4tZwfgrHOc3mvqYlEYSvVi) ’s “Get Lucky (feat. Pharrell Williams and Nile Rodgers)” was omnipresent after its release in 2013. More than a few Spotifiers wrote in to share how the track became part of their—and our—history.


### **Giovanni T • Staff Engineer, Platform**


It was May 2013, and this song was everywhere. It reminds me of the day I joined my dream company—and of moving to Sweden from Italy, which changed my life completely.


### **Josh B • Product Director**


2013 was my first year at Spotify. That summer, the company threw its first big gathering in Stockholm. Whispers bounced around the office about who might perform, and one name kept coming up: Daft Punk.


The night arrived. The energy was already buzzing when the lights dropped, and two figures in gleaming helmets walked onto the stage. The opening of “Get Lucky” hit the speakers and the room exploded.


A song or two later, they took off their helmets and revealed themselves as Spotify employees. It was a perfect fake-out.


That song became the soundtrack to my first year at Spotify: new job, new city, new teammates, and a summer in Stockholm I’ll never forget. Even now, whenever it comes on, I turn it up and get pulled right back to that party.


### **Alberto NA • Senior Engineering Manager, Experience**


I joined Spotify in 2013, and five days later,


[Random Access Memories](https://open.spotify.com/album/4m2880jivSbbyEGAKfITCa) was released. I listened to it nonstop during my first months at the company. It was the perfect kickoff to my first summer in Sweden.


### **Laura K • Senior Director, Global Marketing**


The summer Daft Punk released “Get Lucky,” it was inescapable, inside Spotify and out. Our in-house jam-band The Blacklist covered it to raucous effect at Summer Jam in Stockholm that year, and some people even crowd-surfed. I’ll never forget it.


### **Bryan J • Head of Artist and Industry Partnerships International**


One hazy Stockholm evening in 2013, I heard “Get Lucky” playing outside. I looked up and saw a double rainbow stretching across the sky, and managed to catch it on camera. It was a bit on the nose, but it stuck with me. More than a decade later, it still sums up how it felt to join Spotify at that time: optimistic, slightly surreal, and full of possibility.
